lead: people ring you when they are one conversation away from the thing they have been circling for six years. by the following spring they have done it, and you could not say what week you last thought about them.
sun: in a friendship your hands make the first piece of somebody else's move — the letter drafted at your table, the number found on a saturday, the viewing arranged from your phone on the way home. it exists by monday and belongs to them by monday, and after that it runs on their legs. none of it was charity. being interested in a person comes out of you as work done for them.
moon: the appetite is for the situation that has not resolved — the part they have not said out loud, the thing they are calling fine. that is what brings you in close, fast, and it is genuine for as long as it lasts. the move answers the question. so the hunger goes flat in the same fortnight they are most grateful, and nothing in you clocks the timing at all.
pull: the friendships that turned somebody's life ran about eleven months each. the two that have lasted thirty years are with people whose lives you never got close enough to alter.
tension: six months on they are solid and want to do something back, and find nothing to take hold of: you present as stuck to nobody, and a stuck person is the only kind you know how to be useful to. so the gratitude has nowhere to go. it settles on them as an obligation neither of you named, and each one decides privately that you keep people at a distance.
cost: somebody stuck for six years goes over the line inside a fortnight, and it holds, because the thing made that evening was small and in their hands by the end of it. the closeness had a term on it that neither of you agreed. every life you have turned was turned by a person already halfway out of the room, and the turn keeps, and the friendship does not.

lead: the hall knows one thing about you and it lasted about four minutes. everything else you put into that place arrived with no person attached to it and has been running under other people's arrangements since.
sun: twelve years of starting things there and the building holds no trace of any of it. the rota, the wording on the door, the way the money gets counted on a sunday — each left your hands inside a month and went in under whoever was carrying it. that portability is why they survived, and why the place's account of itself begins after you.
moon: one evening in that room did not disperse. it went out at the only volume available, whole, in front of everybody standing there, and it fixed itself to the person who did it instead of travelling on into the work. what you make detaches, which is why none of it is on you. that did not detach.
pull: everything you made travelled away and stopped being yours. the item still fastened to you is four minutes you never intended to produce, and the room has kept it exactly.
tension: you are careful in that hall now, permanently, in a way you are nowhere else — level voice, questions rather than statements, out by nine. it does not read as restraint to anyone who was not standing there; it reads as cold, or as somebody who never much cared for the place. the four minutes cannot be answered by behaving well for eleven years, because good behaviour leaves no mark either, and marks are the only things kept.
cost: things you make go into a room in a form nobody has to be talked into carrying — no launch, no persuading, people simply doing it differently by the spring. that same lack of grip is why none of it comes back to you. what stuck, stuck because it went in at a size nobody could absorb, and that is the whole of what the place has of you.

lead: eleven years away, and the thursday night is still running, in a better room, with a boy of nineteen explaining to you the rule you invented on the pavement outside to settle an argument nobody there remembers having.
sun: what you started was never an object, and an object is what a person comes back to. the shape of the evening, the rule, the order things happen in — all of it came loose inside the first season and got carried by people with no reason to mention where it came from. it survived because it could travel without you, and it travels still.
moon: nothing in you has ever filed a departure as the end of something, so the leaving was arranged, privately, as an interval. five things are out there in that condition — left in good order, still going, all of them warm toward you. the second time keeps arriving, reliably, and keeps arriving as a visit.
pull: you can walk back into any of the five and be glad to be there. none has a place for you, because a place is the exact thing you built each one not to need.
tension: they tell you the beginning of it wrong, to your face, warmly, and their version works better for them than the accurate one. correcting it would mean taking something back in front of people who would have to rearrange the whole story. so it stands, and you come again next year, and everyone reads that as fondness for an old haunt, while what you are doing is testing whether the door gives onto a room you can be in.
cost: what you start has never needed you in order to keep going, and most started things die with whoever started them. eleven years in a place buys other people a chair; yours bought a procedure nobody needs explained any more. you are welcome in five rooms that would not exist without you, and at home in none of them.

lead: the way you love a person is by making them things, and he died on a wednesday, and the whole apparatus swung round and found nothing standing in front of it.
sun: the hands did not stop. they landed on whatever was still attached to him — the shed rebuilt before the funeral, the accounts taken over, the van sold for what it was worth, his daughter's application done over two evenings at your table. four years of it, none of it announced anywhere, all of it the work you would have done for him if he were there to hand it to.
moon: there was never an edge on the amount, and grief supplies no edge either. what leaves you here has no shape that can be seen from any distance, so the family's account is that you took it well and made yourself useful. they are describing the visible part. the rest went out the way everything else does, unmetered, into people who did not know they were being carried.
pull: grief here has nothing to brace against. it goes sideways into his household as work, at a size nobody has seen, and the one who could have put a figure on it is dead.
tension: four years on, the family's version is that you were practical about it, and the ones who wept are the ones they call closest to him. the only account you could give of your own mourning is a list of jobs, and a list of jobs read out in that kitchen would arrive as an invoice. so it stays unsaid, and in the spring you rebuilt the fence at the back of the house.
cost: a household in the year after a death does not tip over if you are in it — the money straightened, the boy kept in school, the mornings holding their shape, and nobody able to point at where any of that came from. you were never one of the mourners in four years. everything that would have been grief got spent as work, on time, on his people.
